title: Reduction and derived Nakayama
statement:
The finite quotient coefficient has the perfect resolution
$[\mathcal O_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,X}]$, so $K_n$ is the cone of
$\pi_E^n\colon K\to K$. If a derived-complete complex has $K_1=0$, it is zero.
Consequently a morphism between derived-complete complexes is an isomorphism
whenever its first derived reduction is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The finite coefficient quotient has the two-term finite free resolution over $\mathcal O_E$ given by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect], with the notation $\varpi=\pi_E$. The exact sequence of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] gives the corresponding resolution on $X_{\Proet}$: the complex $P_n=[\mathcal O_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,X}]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with augmentation the reduction to $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, is a quasi-isomorphism, so $P_n$ represents $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X[0]$. Its terms in degrees $-1,0$ are free of rank one over $\mathcal O_{E,X}$, with all other terms zero. Hence $P_n$ is perfect in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] for the ringed site $(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_{E,X})$: for every object $V$ take the one-member covering $\{V\to V\}$ and the identity quasi-isomorphism of $P_n|_V$, a bounded complex whose terms $\mathcal O_{E,V}=\mathcal O_{E,V}^{\oplus1}$ are finite free (package data $N_r=1$, $i_r=p_r=\mathrm{id}$ in degrees $-1,0$). The same statement of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] identifies $K_n$ naturally with the cone of $\pi_E^n\colon K\to K$.

source.place: node det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution and the finite-free resolution clause of lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect

proof.text: If $K$ is derived complete and $K_1=0$, the vanishing assertion of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction] gives $K_n=0$ for every $n\geq1$ and $K=0$.

For a morphism $f\colon K\to L$ of derived-complete complexes whose first derived reduction $f_1$ is an isomorphism, the final assertion of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction] directly gives that $f$ is an isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem reduction_and_derived_nakayama (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] : (∃ d : End (Mod.regular (integerRing l E)), (∀ (S : Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ) (f : (integerRing l E).obj.obj S) (s : S.unop), ((d.hom.hom.app S) f).down s = Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E * f.down s) ∧ ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ), (∃ (P : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ), P.IsStrictlyGE (-1) ∧ P.IsStrictlyLE 0 ∧ ∃ (em : P.X (-1) ≅ Mod.regular (AdicCompletion.ring l E X)) (e0 : P.X 0 ≅ Mod.regular (AdicCompletion.ring l E X)), P.d (-1) 0 = em.hom ≫ (regularPullbackIso l E X).inv ≫ (pullback l E X).map (d ^ (n + 1)) ≫ (regularPullbackIso l E X).hom ≫ e0.inv ∧ ∃ ε : P ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) 0).obj (AdicCompletion.finiteModule l E X n), QuasiIso ε ∧ ε.f 0 = e0.hom ≫ AdicCompletion.finiteUnit l E X n) ∧ Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ reductionFunctor l E X (n + 1) ≅ coneFunctor l E X (d ^ (n + 1)))) ∧ (∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (K : Derived l E X), IsDerivedComplete l E X K → IsZero ((reductionFunctor l E X 1).obj K) → IsZero K) ∧ (∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (K L : Derived l E X) (f : K ⟶ L), IsDerivedComplete l E X K → IsDerivedComplete l E X L → IsIso ((reductionFunctor l E X 1).map f) → IsIso f)
